definitions.explanation: Physical or metaphorical space that allows for something additional.
The potential or opportunity for something to occur or be done.

examples.japanese: もう{座|すわ}る{余地|よち}もない。
examples.english: There isn't even room to sit down anymore.

examples.japanese: この{棚|たな}にはもう{本|ほん}を{入|い}れる{余地|よち}がない。
examples.english: There is no more room on this shelf to put books.

examples.japanese: {改善|かいぜん}の{余地|よち}がある。
{疑|うたが}う{余地|よち}はない。
examples.english: There is no room for doubt.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}の{余地|よち}が{残|のこ}されている。
examples.english: There is still room for negotiation.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{余|よ} (extra, surplus) + {地|ち} (ground, space)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜の{余地|よち}がある - there is room for ~
・〜の{余地|よち}がない - there is no room for ~
・〜の{余地|よち}を{残|のこ}す - to leave room for ~

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{改善|かいぜん}の{余地|よち} - room for improvement
・{議論|ぎろん}の{余地|よち} - room for debate
・{疑|うたが}いの{余地|よち} - room for doubt
・{交渉|こうしょう}の{余地|よち} - room for negotiation
・{選択|せんたく}の{余地|よち} - room for choice

NUANCE:
Often used in formal or written contexts to discuss possibilities or limitations.
